claim: CoT helps mainly on math and symbolic tasks; little or nothing on knowledge and commonsense items
note: Sprague meta-analysis (100+ papers) is the anchor; Liu (deliberation hurts) and Stechly (planning gains need specific prompts) agree in direction. a/b/c lines are re-fetches of the same paper, not independent.

claim: CoT can lower accuracy on tasks where deliberation also hurts humans (implicit learning, exceptions, faces)
note: One study, 6 tasks, 3 with large drops. Matches our BrainTeaser/ARC result but not independently replicated. Largest drop 36.3 points, o1-preview vs GPT-4o.

claim: For modern reasoning models explicit CoT prompting gives marginal gains and costs many more tokens
note: Preprint, abstract only. Credibility 70.

claim: Reasoning models overthink easy problems and lose accuracy past a complexity threshold; standard models win at low complexity
note: Shojaee (preprint, methodology disputed publicly) and Chen overthinking (preprint). Both preprints, so moderate.

claim: Longer reasoning can reduce accuracy (inverse scaling) on distractor, spurious-feature and constraint-tracking tasks
note: Gema (synthetic tasks) plus Shojaee collapse. Different mechanisms; synthetic tasks limit transfer. Supports a thinking-length cap.

claim: Models are fragile to irrelevant clauses: one added relevant-looking clause cut accuracy by up to 65%
note: Mirzadeh GSM-Symbolic, abstract only. Supports a strip-distractors step, not tested as a fix.

claim: Self-consistency gains are largest on arithmetic and shrink elsewhere (+17.9 GSM8K, +6.4 StrategyQA, +3.9 ARC-c)
note: Only Wang et al. in this set, old models. Not independently replicated here.

claim: Adaptive stopping cuts self-consistency cost by up to 7.9x with under 0.1 point loss
note: One paper, 17 datasets, 3 LLMs. Open-task accuracy not tested.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction (no external feedback) on reasoning does not help and can hurt
note: Huang, Kamoi survey, Stechly (two papers), Olausson agree. Strongest finding in the set.

claim: Self-correction works when reliable external feedback exists (tests, verifier, ground truth)
note: Kamoi survey, Stechly sound verifier, Olausson, Reflexion (external or simulated feedback). Fits our checkable-task finding.

claim: The bottleneck of self-correction is finding the error, not fixing it
note: Tyen (error location given -> good repair) and Olausson (feedback quality limits repair). Suggests locate-then-fix with an external locator.

claim: Self-Refine style self-feedback gains (about 20%) conflict with later negative results
note: Madaan reports +20% average; Huang says earlier gains came from oracle labels or weak first prompts (12-c-02 is a snippet). Unresolved which tasks or prompts explain it.

claim: LLM judges favor their own outputs, so self-judging is biased
note: Panickssery preprint, abstract only; consistent with 12-c-06.

claim: Repeated sampling raises coverage log-linearly (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples) but without a verifier, selection plateaus
note: Brown et al. only. Coverage is not pick accuracy.

claim: Compute allocated per problem by difficulty beats uniform best-of-N (over 4x efficiency); a small model with search can beat a 14x larger one only where it already has non-trivial success
note: Snell (PRM, MATH) and Wu (7B tree search beats 34B on MATH). Both math with trained verifiers; transfer to open tasks unknown.

claim: Process supervision beats outcome supervision for verifying math steps
note: Lightman only; needs a trained PRM with 800k labels. Not usable by a prompt-only agent.

claim: Tree of Thoughts gives large gains where partial states are cheap to score (Game of 24: 4% to 74%)
note: One paper; no equal-compute control in the abstract; one headline task.

claim: Multi-agent debate does not reliably beat self-consistency or other prompting; multi-agent systems often give minimal gains
note: Smit, Cemri (preprint), Huang (via snippet). Smit counted once. Relevant because we use one agent.

claim: Stated CoT is often unfaithful to the real cause of the answer; reasoning models reveal used hints in under 20% of cases
note: Turpin, Lanham, Chen (Anthropic). Do not treat written reasoning as an audit trail; verify by outcome.

claim: Errors across related models and samples are correlated (about 60% same wrong answer when both err)
note: Kim et al. 2025, one leaderboard. Matches our own measurement and Brown's plateau.

claim: Models of 3B parameters or fewer benefit less from long CoT; short chains fit better
note: One fine-tuning study, not prompting. Low relevance to Sonnet or Haiku class models.

claim: Budget forcing (Wait) on a fine-tuned model raised AIME24 from 50% to 57%; gain depends on fine-tuning
note: Preprint, one model. Prompt-only analog untested.

claim: Prompt-level strategy steps (step-back, plan-and-solve, analogical, self-discover) beat plain zero-shot CoT on benchmarks
note: Four papers agree in direction, but baselines are plain or older CoT, compute is not matched, and Sprague and Meincke say CoT variants matter little on modern models. Unproven for modern models.

claim: Long-conversation memory: long context and RAG help but lag humans
note: LoCoMo only; off the main topic.

claim: Zero-shot think-step-by-step and few-shot CoT gave large gains on early large models
note: Wei and Kojima; old models (540B PaLM, davinci-002). Modern models reason by default, so these gains no longer apply (see Meincke).
